make.name: Mercedes-Benz
make.description: German luxury carmaker. Its electric cars were sold under the EQ sub-brand (EQA, EQB, EQC, EQE, EQS) from 2019; from 2025 new electric models such as the CLA, GLC and C-Class carry their regular names with an electric drivetrain. Mercedes-Benz also co-owns the smart brand with Geely.

models.name: EQS Sedan
models.description: Mercedes-Benz's flagship electric sedan on the dedicated EVA2 platform, launched in 2021. A 2024 facelift brought a larger 118 kWh battery, and a 2026 update moved the car to an 800-volt system with 112 or 122 kWh packs and up to 350 kW charging.

generations.name: Original
generations.description: First EQS on the EVA2 platform with a 107.8 kWh usable battery (108.4 kWh from mid-2023) and 200 kW DC charging.

generations.name: Facelift
generations.description: Facelift with a chrome-slatted grille panel and stand-up star, and a larger 118 kWh usable battery for most versions.

generations.name: 800-volt update
generations.description: Second update (shown April 2026): 800-volt electrics, 112 or 122 kWh batteries, new in-house motors with a two-speed rear transmission, up to 350 kW DC charging and a NACS port in North America.

models.name: EQS SUV
models.description: Electric SUV with an optional third row on the EVA2 platform, on sale since late 2022. The battery grew from 108.4 to 118 kWh for 2024; the Mercedes-Maybach EQS 680 SUV was the luxury version until 2026.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Launched with a 108.4 kWh usable battery; 2024 models moved to 118 kWh. For 2026 the US 450 4MATIC and 580 4MATIC were renamed 400 4MATIC and 550 4MATIC with the same outputs, and the rear-drive 450+ was dropped in the US.

models.name: EQE Sedan
models.description: Mid-size electric sedan on the EVA2 platform, built in Bremen and Beijing since 2022. Mercedes dropped it from the US lineup after the 2026 model year; reports say production ends in 2026, and the electric E-Class is expected to replace it.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Launched with a 90.6 kWh usable battery (89 kWh in the EQE 300/350); the 350+ moved to 96 kWh for 2024, and 2025 updates raised outputs (sold in the US as the EQE 320+ and 320 4MATIC).

models.name: EQE SUV
models.description: Two-row electric SUV on the EVA2 platform, built in Tuscaloosa and Beijing since late 2022. It stays in the US lineup for 2027 as the EQE 320+ and 320 4MATIC SUV.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Shorter-wheelbase SUV sibling of the EQE sedan. For 2024 the 350+ and 500 4MATIC moved to a 96 kWh battery; 2025 updates raised outputs and the US names changed to 320+ and 320 4MATIC for 2026.

variants.name: EQE 320+ SUV (2025 update; EQE 350+ SUV in Europe)

models.name: EQB
models.description: Compact electric SUV with an optional third row, based on the GLB, sold from 2021. Mercedes removed it from European configurators in September 2025 and ended US and Canadian sales after the 2025 model year; the electric GLB replaces it.

generations.name: Original
generations.description: First EQB, front motor or dual-motor 4MATIC with a 66.5 kWh usable battery; the long-range 250+ (70.5 kWh) arrived in 2022.

generations.name: Facelift
generations.description: Facelift with a new grille panel and interior tech; all versions use the 70.5 kWh battery in the US.

models.name: EQA
models.description: Compact electric SUV based on the GLA, built in Rastatt and Beijing from 2021 and never sold in the US. Orders closed in March 2026 and production ended in mid-2026; the new electric GLA replaces it.

generations.name: Original
generations.description: Front-drive EQA 250 and dual-motor 300/350 4MATIC with a 66.5 kWh usable battery; the 250+ (70.5 kWh) followed in 2022.

generations.name: Facelift
generations.description: Late-2023 facelift with a star-pattern grille panel and updated MBUX; drivetrains carried over.

models.name: EQC
models.description: Mercedes-Benz's first EQ-branded electric car, a mid-size SUV derived from the GLC, built from 2019 to 2023. A planned US launch was cancelled.

generations.name: Original
generations.description: Dual-motor EQC 400 4MATIC with an 80 kWh usable battery.

models.name: G 580 Electric
models.description: Battery-electric version of the G-Class with four wheel motors, a 116 kWh battery and a low-range mode, on sale since 2024. Launched as the G 580 with EQ Technology and renamed G 580 Electric in the US for 2027.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Electric version of the W465 G-Class with four individually controlled motors and a ladder frame with an integrated battery.

models.name: CLA Electric
models.description: Electric version of the third-generation CLA on the MMA platform with 800-volt charging, revealed in 2025. It launched as the CLA with EQ Technology and is called CLA Electric in the US from the 2027 model year.

generations.name: Third generation
generations.description: First car on the MMA platform: rear or dual motors, 85 kWh (58 or 71 kWh in cheaper versions) batteries and up to 320 kW charging.

models.name: CLA Shooting Brake Electric
aliases: CLA Shooting Brake with EQ Technology
models.description: Estate version of the electric CLA on the MMA platform, revealed in 2025 and sold in Europe.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Shooting Brake body on the CLA Electric's MMA platform with the same drivetrains.

models.name: GLC Electric
models.description: Battery-electric GLC on the 800-volt MB.EA-M platform, revealed in September 2025 as the GLC with EQ Technology. US deliveries of the 2027 GLC 400 4MATIC began in the second half of 2026.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: First model on the MB.EA-M platform: 85 or 94 kWh batteries, 800-volt charging at up to 330 kW.

models.name: C-Class Electric
models.description: Battery-electric C-Class sedan on the MB.EA-M platform, unveiled in April 2026, with 800-volt charging. On sale in Europe; US timing not announced as of November 2026.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Electric C-Class sharing the GLC Electric's 800-volt hardware: 85 or 94 kWh batteries, up to 330 kW charging.

models.name: GLB Electric
models.description: Second-generation GLB on the MMA platform, revealed in December 2025 as the GLB with EQ Technology and launched electric-only, with optional seven seats. It replaces the EQB.

generations.name: Second generation
generations.description: MMA-platform GLB with 58, 71 or 85 kWh batteries and rear or dual motors.

models.name: GLA Electric
models.description: Third-generation GLA on the MMA platform, revealed in July 2026 with electric drive and built in Rastatt. It replaces the EQA; the US version is due about a year after Europe.

generations.name: Third generation
generations.description: MMA-platform GLA with 58 or 85 kWh batteries and 800-volt charging.

models.name: Mercedes-AMG GT 4-Door Coupe (electric)
models.description: First model on the AMG.EA platform, revealed in May 2026: axial-flux motors, a 106 kWh 800-volt battery and up to 600 kW DC charging. It replaces the petrol AMG GT 4-Door Coupe.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: AMG.EA platform with two or three axial-flux motors and a 106 kWh usable battery.

models.name: Mercedes-AMG GT SUV
models.description: Second AMG.EA model and AMG's first in-house SUV, revealed in October 2026. Orders opened in Europe for the GT 53 on 20 October 2026; GT 55 and GT 63 follow in spring 2027 and US deliveries in summer 2027.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: AMG.EA SUV with 106 kWh (GT 53) or 128 kWh (GT 55/63) batteries.

models.name: VLE
models.description: Large electric MPV and the first model on the VAN.EA platform, revealed in March 2026 with a 115 kWh battery and 800-volt charging. It replaces the EQV.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: VAN.EA platform with front or dual motors.

models.name: VLS
models.description: Announced luxury MPV on the VAN.EA platform that will sit above the VLE.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Announced; no specifications published as of November 2026.

models.name: EQV
models.description: Electric version of the V-Class MPV, sold in Europe from 2020 and facelifted in 2024. Production ended in 2026 and the VLE replaces it.

generations.name: Original
generations.description: Front-drive EQV 300 with a 90 kWh battery; EQV 250 with 60 kWh from 2021.

generations.name: Facelift
generations.description: V-Class facelift styling and interior update.

models.name: eVito Tourer
models.description: Electric version of the Vito passenger van (up to nine seats), sold in Europe since 2019 with 41, 60 and 90 kWh batteries over its life.

generations.name: Original
generations.description: Launched with a 41 kWh battery (35 kWh usable); a 90 kWh battery came in 2020 and a 60 kWh option in 2022.

generations.name: Facelift
generations.description: Vito facelift styling with 60 or 90 kWh batteries.

models.name: EQT
models.description: Electric small MPV based on the T-Class/Citan (a Renault Kangoo E-Tech twin) with a 45 kWh battery, sold in Europe from 2023. Mercedes announced in April 2025 that the T-Class and EQT would end in 2026.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Front motor with a 45 kWh battery, standard or long body.

models.name: B-Class Electric Drive
models.description: Electric B-Class with a Tesla-supplied battery and motor, sold in the US from 2014 and in Europe as the B 250 e until 2017.

generations.name: Original
generations.description: Front-drive W242 with a 28 kWh usable battery.

models.name: SLS AMG Coupe Electric Drive
models.description: Battery-electric version of the SLS AMG gullwing coupe with four wheel motors and a 60 kWh battery, built to order in very small numbers in 2013.

generations.name: Original
generations.description: Four motors (one per wheel), 60 kWh battery, 552 kW.

models.name: A-Class E-Cell
models.description: Electric version of the second-generation A-Class built at Rastatt from September 2010; about 500 were leased to customers in Europe as a demonstration programme rather than sold.

generations.name: Original
generations.description: W169 A-Class with a 36 kWh battery and a 70 kW front motor.

models.name: Vito E-Cell
models.description: Electric Vito panel van and the first series-built electric Mercedes-Benz van, built from 2010 and discontinued in 2012 for low demand.

generations.name: Original
generations.description: 36 kWh battery (32 kWh usable), 60 kW continuous and 70 kW peak motor.

models.name: eVito Panel Van
models.description: Electric Vito cargo van sold in Europe since 2018, first with an 85 kW motor and from the 2024 facelift with a 150 kW motor and 60 or 90 kWh batteries.

generations.name: Original
generations.description: 85 kW front motor (2018-2020).

generations.name: Facelift
generations.description: Facelift with the 150 kW motor from the EQV and 60 or 90 kWh batteries.

models.name: eSprinter
models.description: Electric Sprinter large van. The first version (2019-2023) used 41 or 55 kWh batteries; the second, sold in Europe and North America since 2023 and built in Germany and South Carolina, offers up to 113 kWh usable.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Front motor of 85 kW with 35 or 47 kWh usable batteries.

generations.name: Second generation
generations.description: Rear-drive electric platform with 81 or 113 kWh usable batteries and 100 kW or 150 kW motors; US production in Ladson, South Carolina.

models.name: eCitan
models.description: Electric version of the second-generation Citan small van (a Renault Kangoo E-Tech twin), on sale from 2022. Mercedes announced in April 2025 that the Citan, T-Class, eCitan and EQT would end in 2026.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: 90 kW front motor with a 45 kWh battery.

legacy_notes.note: Maybach EQS 680 SUV: $179,900 and 280 mi match the first MY2024 EPA rating; legacy 658 hp is the EU figure (US 649 hp). Discontinued in the US for 2027.
EQS 580 SUV row is MY2023 (108.4 kWh: $125,950, 285 mi). From 2024 the battery is 118 kWh and the US name became EQS 550 4MATIC for 2026.
EQS 450 4MATIC SUV row is MY2023 (108.4 kWh, 285 mi). Renamed EQS 400 4MATIC SUV in the US for 2026 ($89,950).
EQS 450+ SUV row is MY2023 (305 mi). The 450+ SUV was dropped from the US lineup for 2026.
AMG EQS row: $147,550 with 277 mi is MY2022-2023; MY2024 is 305 mi, MY2025 315 mi. The AMG EQS sedan is no longer offered for 2026.
EQS 580 sedan row is MY2023 ($125,950, 340 mi), pre-facelift.
EQS 450 4MATIC sedan row is MY2023 ($107,400, 340 mi), pre-facelift.
EQS 450+ sedan row is MY2023 ($104,400, 350 mi); legacy torque 419 lb-ft is the 2024+ figure (417 before).
Wrong row: labelled EQB 350 4MATIC with 350 power/torque, but price $53,050 and 251 mi are the MY2024 EQB 250+. Claimed on the facelift 350 4MATIC (US $60,850, 207 mi).
EQB 250+ row matches MY2023 ($52,750, 245 mi). The EQB is discontinued (US after MY2025).
AMG EQE SUV: $109,300 is MY2024; legacy 233 mi matches no EPA rating (MY2024 235, MY2025-26 230).
EQE 350+ SUV: legacy 300 mi matches no EPA rating (MY2023 279, MY2024 307, MY2025 302). Replaced by the EQE 320+ SUV in the US for 2026.
EQE 350 4MATIC SUV: legacy 285 mi is wrong (EPA 253 MY2023, 265 MY2024, 253 MY2025).
EQE 500 4MATIC SUV: legacy 286 mi is wrong (EPA 282 MY2024, 264 MY2025). Not offered in the US for 2026.
EQE 350+ sedan row matches MY2023 ($74,900, 305 mi). The EQE sedan leaves the US lineup after MY2026.
AMG EQE sedan: $106,900 is MY2023-2025 and 230 mi is MY2024; MY2026 is $96,600 / 220 mi and the last US year.
EQE 350 4MATIC sedan row matches MY2023 ($77,900, 260 mi).
EQE 500 4MATIC sedan row matches MY2023 ($85,900, 260 mi).

gaps: Make legacy name "Mercedes" should display as "Mercedes-Benz".
EPA ratings missing from the fueleconomy.gov dataset for MY2023 EQE sedan/SUV and MY2023 EQB; MY2023 ranges come from Mercedes-Benz USA spec pages instead; MY2023 EQE 500 4MATIC SUV range not found.
MY2027 EQS 450+ EPA range not yet published; AMG GT 4-Door (electric) US prices not announced; AMG GT 55/63 EPA 320 mi only.
EPA lists two MY2024 Maybach EQS 680 SUV ratings (280 and 321 mi); the first (280) is used.
EPA lists two MY2026 CLA 250+ ratings (317 and 374 mi); 374 mi (the figure Mercedes-Benz USA quotes) is used.
European prices are German list prices from EV Database (last known price for discontinued versions); Chinese-market versions (CLTC range, CNY prices) are not covered.
Ranges and prices for the electric C-Class, GLA, GLB, CLA Shooting Brake, VLE and AMG GT SUV are European only; no US launch data yet.
No US prices sourced for the B-Class Electric Drive or MY2022 AMG EQS; eSprinter and eVito/eCitan specs are partial (no range or price).
Commercial heavy trucks (eActros, eEconic) belong to Daimler Truck, not Mercedes-Benz, and are not included.
Mercedes-Maybach and AMG versions are variants of their base models, except the AMG.EA cars, which are their own models.
No verified photo found for: A-Class E-Cell, eVito Panel Van (2024), eSprinter (both generations), eCitan, VLS (Wikimedia API rate-limited during research).
EQE SUV generation image and four other generations reuse legacy files (viewed; they show the right generation).
Variants with null power/WLTP range are older or minor European versions whose EV Database pages could not be fetched (HTTP 429 rate limit); listing data (battery, 0-100 km/h, price) is filled.
GLC Electric, CLA, GLA, GLB and AMG GT chassis codes (X540, C174, X174, H244, X244, C590, X591) are taken from Wikipedia/Commons naming, not from Mercedes press material.
